findings.reason: a plan that adds a subsystem without citing what it searched will be built as a parallel mechanism beside the one that shipped three days after it was written.
findings.text: §2 ("crew dispatch adds three paths to every implement, test and investigate node without the coordinator declaring them: the node's own plan file, its cumulative evidence record, and a figures directory for the node") does not cite the machinery that already does this. The census of missed prior art: `_grant_landing_write_paths` (dispatch.py:2044) and `_landing_fragment_paths` (dispatch.py:2006), which grant a per-node fragment by default; `_shared_landing_paths` (dispatch.py:1955), which documents the shared grant as removed; `PLAN_LANDING_CONTRACT`/`BRIEF_LANDING_CONTRACT` (reckon/crew/prompts.py:156,193), which already carry the plan landing contract text §4 says it will add; the refusal registry `DISPATCH_REFUSAL_REMEDIES` (reckon/crew/refusals.py:18); and the landing-record owner `reckon/_store.py:924` / `reckon/evidence.py:503`. §4 also cites `skills/reckon-ship`, which does not exist (skills are reckon-build, -create, -edit, -roadmap, -sprint, -status, -sync) — the contract text lives in `reckon/crew/prompts.py`.

findings.reason: the section must extend the fragment default rather than fork the superseded shared grant, and must state which of the two incompatible figures semantics it means.
findings.text: §2 reintroduces the shared plan-file-plus-evidence-record grant that `_shared_landing_paths` deliberately removed; its docstring states the fragment default exists precisely because "a grant every node holds is exactly the merge conflict the per-node fragment default removes". The owner to extend is `_landing_fragment_paths`/`_grant_landing_write_paths` (dispatch.py:2006,2044), landed in f6e41cc7d (2026-09-28). §2 as written would for two of its three paths re-create the add/add conflict the fragment design eliminates, and its own 2026-09-18 comment (c-the-default-scope-makes-a-promotion-refusal-routine) already measured that exact collision. The plan's "figures directory for the node" is also already the fragment's `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/`.

findings.reason: the honest change is an extension of the fragment grant and the promotion gate, and saying so is what keeps §3 from being a parallel check beside the existing commit gate.
findings.text: §2's grant is a thin layer over the existing per-node fragment grant and §3's "commits touch neither the plan nor the evidence record" is a thin layer over promotion's existing commit-vs-worktree machinery (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:2539`), with the landing record path owned at `reckon/_store.py:924`. The plan states no reason the existing grant and landing machinery cannot be extended; its §3 escape, §2's opt-out, and the refusal it adds are all expressed as new surface rather than extensions of the owners.

findings.reason: the plan must account for the interface surface it adds — naming which family the two new refusals join and whether `--no-record` subsumes or parallels `--no-commit` — or drop the additions.
findings.text: against this week's figures (public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23), §2 adds a `crew dispatch` refusal family (a brief whose text scopes the record out is refused) and §3 adds the `--no-record REASON` CLI option plus a `crew complete` refusal and a figures warning; no section in the plan names anything it retires or merges, and none states why nothing can be. The existing registry at `reckon/crew/refusals.py:18` (D01–D23) is where a new family must be registered, and the plan's §3 deliberately mirrors the existing `--no-commit`.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no new module; it edits existing dispatch (scope resolution), promotion (gate) and view surfaces, so there is no new shallow wrapper over shared machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements landing-path granting rather than extending its owner, and its new refusals, if added ad hoc, fork the refusal registry.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1481, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 adds a `crew dispatch` refusal family and §3 adds a `--no-record REASON` CLI option plus a `crew complete` refusal, and neither section names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 proposes a default grant of the plan file, evidence record and figures directory without citing `_grant_landing_write_paths`/`_landing_fragment_paths` (dispatch.py:2044/2006), which already grant each node its own landing fragment by default.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2's three-path grant is a thin layer over the existing per-node fragment grant and §3's record-touch check a thin layer over promotion's landing machinery, with no statement of why the existing grant cannot be extended.
